pr_title: intel_adsp: fix boot errors with no_optimizations
pr_body:
Certain boot functions were not stored in IMR, higher opt levels inlined
them so issues weren't noticed. Also, a power managment sys_write32
halts execution, this needs to be resolved before merging. So far, only
tested on hello_world sample, full SOF fails at the moment.

Signed-off-by: Noah Klayman <noah.klayman@intel.com>

Fixes #48390

TODO:

- [x] Determine issue with power management sys_write32 and use a better solution than commenting it out
- [ ] Verify something more complex than hello_world works (All the issues have been before application code, but other configurations could potentially cause issues)
- [ ] I'm not 100% sure I correctly implemented the effect of the `__imr` macro for `z_soc_mp_asm_entry`, can someone verify this?
pr_comments: @ceolin  Can you take a look at this? The PM call is failing in O0.

> @ceolin Can you take a look at this? The PM call is failing in O0.

Yep, I can take a look. This is not part of Zephyr's PM logic though. This is  soc initialization.

Rebased on latest main and found that I could uncomment the `sys_write32` commented out without issue (at least for `hello_world`). Ran a test workload with CAVS25, it seems to be doing fine even with intensive tests (though I plan to try the kernel tests on 0O with the three boards to see what'll happen). 

I've asked @teburd if he can take a look and verify the IMR. I'm currently fighting to build and boot SOF so I can verify this works for SOF too. Having issues with cavstool Twister.

>  if he can take a look and verify the IMR. I'm currently fighting to build and boot SOF so I can verify this works for SOF too. Having issues with cavstool Twister.

I don't think anyone ever loads SOF with cavstool. Stick to what is heavily tested many times a day: load SOF from the kernel driver and then call `cavstool --log-only`

issue_context.title: [Intel Cavs] Boot failures on low optimization levels
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Compiling at low optimization levels causes boot failures with both XCC and GCC toolchains across cavs platforms (tested 18 and 25, assume other platforms are affected as well). Specifically, O0 and O1 fail with XCC, while only O0 fails with GCC.

**To Reproduce**
Essentially, build and run and zephyr application on a cavs platform with O0 or O1 for XCC or O0 for GCC. Simple steps below:

1. set `CONFIG_NO_OPTIMIZATIONS=y` in hello_world prj.conf (and optionally change `compiler_flags.cmake` to force O1 instead of O0 if you'd like to test that)
**Edit for clarification:** The boot failure does not depend on the kconfig no_optimizations value. Hardcoding O0 into the optimize_speed causes a failure, and hardcoding O2 (or O1 for GCC) into no_optimizations results in a successful boot.
2. `west build -b intel_adsp_cavs18 samples/hello_world`
3. sign binary (`west sign -t rimage --tool-path=[path to /build-rimage/rimage] -D [path to sof/rimage/config] -- -k [path to sof/keys/otc_private_key.pem]`)
4. boot with cavstool
5. see incorrect FW status and no logged message

**Expected behavior**
Hello World log message should be printed

**Impact**
Causes problems when trying to debug as I'm forced to use high optimization levels.

**Logs and console output** (from GCC with O0)
[build_log.txt](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/9204073/build_log.txt)

Cavstool output:

comments:
> Edit for clarification: The boot failure does not depend on the kconfig no_optimizations value. Hardcoding O0 into the optimize_speed causes a failure, and hardcoding O2 (or O1 for GCC) into no_optimizations results in a successful boot.

So this is making sure that there's absolutely zero CMake or Kconfiguration problem but really just an issue with the actual optimization level, and only with the optimization level correct? Did you inspect the compiler command lines with `ninja clean; ninja -v &> build.log` in all cases?

Yep. With XCC, I built with no_optimizations twice, with the second time hardcoding it to use O2. The build logs were identical except for the the optimization levels passed to GCC. However, only the second build successfully booted. They were also nearly identical with GCC, but there was an extra warning printed by O0.

Looks like this was caused by boot functions not being in the imr section, O2 would inline them so the issue wasn't noticed. There's also a weird thing with power management. See #48749 for WIP solution, turned out to be quite small (but was a lot of work to discover). Unfortunately, SOF still has its own issues (but gets further than before):

@mmahadevan108 how is a failure to boot priority:low?

(Update for tracking purposes) Setting up to test out Noah's PR and discussing with Flavio.

> @mmahadevan108 how is a failure to boot priority:low?
> 
> EDIT: this seems to be an Intel-only bug BTW

This was given a priority as it was limited to certain platform.
With `-O0` and `-O1`, sometimes you have to enlarge the stack sizes of various threads (e.g. main and interrupt stacks).

> This was given a priority as it was limited to certain platform.

It's very high priority (and severity) for the Intel ADSP which fails to boot. Other platforms should not matter, people who don't care about Intel ADSP should filter out and never even see any intel ADSP bug anyway.

If all platform-specific bugs are automatically low priority then the priority field is  useless for platform-specific bugs.

And of course there's confusion between severity and priority as usual:
- https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/46759

review_comments: The syntax here is fine, but the semantics are surprising.  What on earth is trying to launch a second core before the first has finished the IMR->HPSRAM copy?  That seems like the root cause here, nothing should be touching that code until long, long after we've exited early boot.
Is this fixing the problem for you ? This code path is not exercised if you build with `CONFIG_MP_NUM_CPUS=1` but the boot still fails.

> Is this fixing the problem for you ? This code path is not exercised if you build with `CONFIG_MP_NUM_CPUS=1` but the boot still fails.

Checked and like you said, whether it boots or not with `CONFIG_MP_NUM_CPUS=1`  doesn't depend on this code path. It does boot with the other change in `include/zephyr/arch/xtensa/cache.h`, though:
```
static ALWAYS_INLINE void z_xtensa_cache_flush(void *addr, size_t bytes)
```
